practices.heading: Best practices for Claude
practices.subheading: The COE's distilled playbook for building things that work in production.

category.name: Prompting
category.practice: Treat Claude like a brilliant new teammate: state the goal, the audience and the format. Ambiguity in, ambiguity out.

practice.title: Use XML tags to structure prompts

category.practice: Wrap instructions, context and examples in tags like <context> and <example> so Claude can parse intent reliably.
For hard problems, ask for step-by-step reasoning before the final answer to improve accuracy.
A few high-quality examples (multishot prompting) beat paragraphs of abstract instructions.

category.name: Agents & Tools

practice.title: Start simple, add agency only when needed

category.practice: Prefer a single well-prompted call or a fixed workflow before reaching for a fully autonomous agent.
Clear names, typed parameters and rich descriptions make tool use dramatically more reliable.

practice.title: Keep the human in the loop

category.practice: For irreversible or outward-facing actions, design explicit confirmation steps.
Use the Model Context Protocol to connect tools and data sources in a portable, reusable way.

category.name: Evals & Quality
category.practice: Write down measurable criteria and a representative test set first — then iterate against it.
Use code-graded and model-graded evals so quality is measured, not guessed, on every change.
Include adversarial, ambiguous and empty inputs in your eval set, not just the happy path.

category.name: Cost, Safety & Ops
category.practice: Use prompt caching for system prompts and documents to cut latency and cost significantly.
Match model to task — reserve the most capable models for genuinely hard reasoning.
Add input/output guardrails and least-privilege tool access from day one, not as an afterthought.
